sam: Seeing a perf regression on AMD nodes after yesterday's autotune merge. Long-context requests (seq>1024) jump latency ~2.5x and KV cache hits look lower.
linh: Ugh. Is it consistently on all AMD SKUs or only certain card families? Any errors in the kernel-selector logs?
sam: Only repros on the 7900 series in staging. Prod p99 also showed a bump but less obvious. Kernel-selector log snippet:
```
I2026-03-15T09:12:03Z kernel-selector: selected kernel=matmul_amp_bf16_shard_v2
I2026-03-15T09:12:03Z fallback: no kernel found for seq_len_bucket=2048 -> routing to cpu_gemm
```
sam: Notice the fallback to cpu_gemm when seq_len_bucket >= 2048. Before the autotune we used amdgpu_kern_shard_native and stayed on GPU.
ryan: That fallback is the problem. Looks like the autotuner created a new preferred kernel that isn't available for that seq-length path, so the routing policy falls back all the way to cpu. Can you capture the /var/log/inference/runtime-profile for one request? Quick grep for "fallback" and "kernel_unavailable".
sam: Pasted core excerpt:
```
[profile] request_id=abc123
kernel_probe: available_kernels=[matmul_amp_bf16_shard_v1, matmul_amp_bf16_shard_v2]
compat_check: seq_len=2048 -> compatible_kernels=[]
decision: route=cpu_gemm (latency_est=120ms)
kv_cache: miss_rate=0.12 (expected ~0.02)
```
sam: compat_check returning empty for seq>=2048 even though matmul_amp_bf16_shard_v1 should support it. Might be opcode signature mismatch.
linh: Can you run the kernel inspector on the staging image? `./tools/rocm-kernel-inspector --list --filter=matmul` and also `--check-signatures`.
sam: Ran it. Output:
```
matmul_amp_bf16_shard_v1: arch=gfx1030, max_seq=4096, signature=matmul_v1
matmul_amp_bf16_shard_v2: arch=gfx1030, max_seq=1024, signature=matmul_v2
```
sam: v2 has max_seq=1024 which explains the gap. Autotune picked v2 for common cases, but didn't register v1 as compatible for the >=1024 bucket.
eva: Is this an autotune metadata bug then? The registry should mark both as compatible if arch matches and max_seq allows. Maybe the signature comparer is too strict (requires exact signature equality) instead of subset superset logic.
ryan: Yep. The autotuner writes a kernel_manifest.json during build. I suspect the manifest for v1 got an incorrect signature after we refactored the build flags. Quick workaround: add a conditional routing rule to prefer matmul_amp_bf16_shard_v1 for seq_len>=1024 on gfx1030 until we fix the manifest.
sam: Proposed small policy patch (will open PR):
```
routing_policies:
  - match: { arch: gfx1030, seq_len_min: 1024 }
    prefer: ["matmul_amp_bf16_shard_v1"]
```
linh: Good. Also add a diagnostic to log available_kernels + claimed_max_seq for the bucket so we can trace next time.
ops-bot: deploy-bot: patch/2345 applied to staging (sam) — rollout started :rocket:
eva: We should also add a unit test in autotune that validates manifest.max_seq >= highest_bucket it claims to support. That would have caught this.
sam: Agreed. Filing followups: 1) quick routing patch to staging (in PR), 2) autotune manifest test + fix build flags, 3) postmortem note & perf regression alert rule.
ryan: For immediate verification, can someone run a micro-benchmark: `./bin/infer --model gpt-xx --seq 2048 --gpu-type gfx1030 --repeat 50` and attach runtime-profile? I can compare kernel selection traces.
sam: Running now, will attach results in a min.
linh: Thx. If this is urgent for prod, we can also add an emergency fallback to prefer any gpu kernel over cpu_gemm when latency delta > 3x. But be careful about correctness.
eva: Add a metric for "kernel_unexpected_cpu_fallback" to catch this class of regressions.
sam: Results attached: p99 dropped from 320ms -> 98ms after the routing override. KV miss_rate back to 0.03. Looks like the routing fix helps.
linh: Nice. Keep the PR small. We'll revert once manifest/build fix is in.
ryan: I'll own the manifest test. eva, can you own the metric/alert?
eva: Yep, filing tickets.
sam: Thanks all. Follow-ups in #eng-runtime backlog. :thumbsup:
